newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-NORMAN LEADS HUNT FOR GOLF'S RICHEST JACKPOT.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-NORMAN LEADS HUNT FOR GOLF'S RICHEST JACKPOT.

text.p: World number one Greg Norman leads four regional champions from around the world into battle for golf's richest jackpot at the $3.65 million World Championship of Golf beginning Saturday at the Grayhawk Golf Club.

The match-play competition will feature Norman, the International champion; Scott Hoch, the U.S. champion; Briton Sam Torrance, the European champion; and Hisayuki Sasaki, the Japanese champion. Each of them won three matches in their respective regions to earn a berth in the semifinals.
Norman will take on Sasaki, and Hoch will battle Torrance in Saturday's semifinals. The winners will play 36 holes in Sunday's final over the 7,001-yard, par-72 Grayhawk Golf Club.
First prize is $1 million, while the runner-up receives $500,000. England's Barry Lane defeated Frost, 2-up, in last year's championship final.

Norman, golf's all-time money-winner with nearly $10.5 million, defeated fellow-Australian Craig Parry, former PGA Champion Steve Elkington and last year's finalist, David Frost, to win in the International bracket.
Hoch, who had his first $1 million season in 1996, beat British Open champion Tom Lehman, Mark McCumber and 1993 U.S. Open champion Lee Janzen to earn a trip to Scottsdale.
Torrance, an eight-time Ryder Cup member and winner of over 20 events on the European Tour, topped Mark James, Miguel Angel Jimenez and world No. 4 Colin Montgomerie in the European region.
Sasaki, a member of the Japan Tour since 1986, defeated last year's Japanese champion, Massy Kuramoto, Hideki Kase and Shigeki Maruyama to win his region.
